transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Time: 15:30 UTC (08:30 PT)
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Veridian Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng), Sourav Bose (Data Privacy), J. Lee (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Quick review of pilot metrics: latency regressions on long prompts observed with model v2.0, candidate v2.1 shows better throughput but cost delta unclear.
- Agreement to pin v2.1 for evaluation run + shadow routing test.
- Security questions around KMS and audit logs; customer to provide requirements.
- Action items: 10k prompt run, pricing sheet, privacy checklist review, schedule shadow test.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, quick roll call — we've got the weekly pilot sync for Veridian. Diego and I are on from Redwood. Anika, you wanna start with context?
[00:12] Anika Patel: yeah, hi all, thanks. Um, quick recap — we ran the mixed workload for two days, about 50k tokens per day, and we saw tail latency spikes on the older pinned v2.0 model, especially for our 1k+ token clinical summarization prompts.
[00:27] Tom Reynolds: and to add, those spikes were mostly on the longer sequences, like the 4k step transcripts. The bulk throughput is fine but p99 is annoying.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: okay, makes sense. On our side we observed blocking in the KV cache lookups leading to some stalls—sometimes metric called k-v cash locking, the instrumentation's raw but shows hot shards.
[00:48] Anika Patel: right, and we think those are symptomatic of the model weights memory layout, maybe quantization mismatch?
[00:54] Diego Alvarez: yeah it could be layout + batch packing. The newer v2.1 has a slightly different kernel path that's more quantization-friendly. We tested a small bench and it improved p95 by about 18% for the long prompts.
[01:10] Maya Chen: and the cost delta there? That was one of their main asks last week—if v2.1 is faster, is it also cheaper per token or similar?
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: initial bench shows marginally higher GPU cycles per token but because of reduced tail latency and fewer retries the end-to-end cost per completed request should be lower. Need to run the full 10k suite to be sure.
[01:28] Anika Patel: ok let's do the 10k then. We'll pin traffic for the eval and do shadow routing for a 5% slice to compare production vs pinned v2.1 outputs.
[01:36] J. Lee: quick product note — we care about deterministic outputs for auditability, so model version pinning is non-negotiable for the next phase.
[01:44] Sourav Bose: on privacy, we need to confirm KMS integration plus HSM support. Also SOC2 logs, like who called what model and full audit chain—do you have that?
[01:54] Maya Chen: yes, we have audit logs and SSO/SAML integrations. We'll share the security checklist. For KMS/HSM, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys and HSM-based wrapping—I'll add the specifics to the doc.
[02:06] Tom Reynolds: and can we have per-route retention, like keep inference logs for 90 days for some routes and 7 days for others?
[02:11] Diego Alvarez: yep, the console supports route-level retention policies and token-level anonymization. There are also workspace-level defaults.
[02:19] Anika Patel: good. On model fallback, we want safe degraded paths if v2.1 is unavailable. What are the options?
[02:25] Diego Alvarez: you can configure soft failover to a smaller model variant—call it v2.1-lite— or hard fallback to v1.8. We also support automatic region fallback and queueing strategies. Important to test on traffic choreography.
[02:38] J. Lee: any risks with output drift between pinned v2.1 and fallback v1.8? We don't want two different behaviors in prod.
[02:44] Maya Chen: good point. Typical pattern is to use deterministic postprocessors and an eval suite to detect drift. For critical routes we recommend canarying and an automatic rollback if the quality delta exceeds threshold X.
[02:56] Anika Patel: what about checksum or fingerprinting the model responses? We need to detect subtle semantic regressions.
[03:02] Diego Alvarez: we can compute embedding distances per response and aggregate. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions on a prompt-level. Also, you can pin prompt sets as golden prompts to trigger alerts.
[03:16] Tom Reynolds: for the shadow routing test, operationally how do we capture end-to-end latency without affecting user experience?
[03:22] Maya Chen: shadow routing is asynchronous — you fork a copy of the request to the pinned model and collect outputs and telemetry. It doesn't contribute to production latency. We'll ensure the shadow path is rate-limited to 5% and stored in a separate trace.
[03:34] Anika Patel: okay. One thing — earlier we saw the Redwood console showing token consumption per user, but our data residency policy requires that traces with PII never leave our VPC. How do we keep shadow logs private?
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: for Private customers we offer an in-VPC collector that writes logs directly to your S3 endpoint or your internal logging. For hosted pilots, we can strip PII or redact at the edge. We'll document that.
[03:56] Sourav Bose: the redact isn't enough for us unless guaranteed—so Private with in-VPC collector is preferred for the next phase.
[04:04] Maya Chen: noted. We'll mark that as requirement in the pilot plan.
[04:10] Anika Patel: timeline check — we're targeting a decision before end of quarter, 2025-12-31, since procurement team is on holidays starting the 26th. Are those dates still realistic?
[04:19] Maya Chen: yes, that's tight but doable. Our action items will be fast-turn. Diego, can you get results by 12/24 as discussed?
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: yes, I'll prioritize the 10k sweep pinned to v2.1 with histogram, cost model estimate, and a few example prompts showing delta.
[04:33] Tom Reynolds: side question — packaging for dedicated vs hosted, is there a delta if we pick dedicated right away? E.g., do we get guaranteed pinned model residency?
[04:41] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and model residency guarantees for the pinned versions, plus SLA for latency. Hosted is faster to start but doesn't guarantee pool isolation. I'll send a matrix after the call.
[04:52] J. Lee: can you include burst options? We have big events where throughput spikes need to be absorbed.
[04:57] Maya Chen: yes, will include burst and autoscale knobs and cost deltas.
[05:02] Anika Patel: any blockers from your side on doing a shadow run in our sandbox?
[05:07] Diego Alvarez: need SSH/API access to the sandbox network or we'll deploy an in-VPC collector. It's standard network setup—Tom, can you share the onboarding ticket?
[05:15] Tom Reynolds: I'll open the ticket with the network details right after the call.
[05:19] Maya Chen: cool. Anything else on rollbacks — we should confirm the rollback surface and how quickly traffic can be moved to fallback.
[05:27] Diego Alvarez: rollback is immediate in config — you update route to pin fallback model and Atomic rollout is supported. For in-flight requests, there's a small window but we can drain gracefully.
[05:36] Anika Patel: we want a 5 minute SLA for rollback to be able to shift traffic in case of a severe regression. Can Redwood support that?
[05:42] Maya Chen: yes, with Dedicated/reserved capacity plus proper runbook we can meet that. We'll document the runbook and the playbook for your SREs.
[05:50] Sourav Bose: ok also, audit — we need immutable logs for model switches and who initiated them. That is note optional.
[05:56] Diego Alvarez: we log operator actions + request traces and tie to SSO identity. Audit export can be sent to your SIEM.
[06:03] Anika Patel: great. last bit — quality thresholds for auto-rollback? we suggested threshold X earlier — let's specify numbers.
[06:10] Maya Chen: propose auto-rollback if p95 latency increases by >30% or embedding distance aggregates show mean semantic drift > 0.12 on the golden set. That's configurable.
[06:22] J. Lee: sounds reasonable. We'll review the golden set composition and send it to Diego.
[06:28] Anika Patel: ok quick recap please so we can close this out.
[06:31] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Diego runs 10k prompt sweep pinned to v2.1 and shares latency/cost histograms by 12/24. 2) Maya will send pricing matrix and burst/dedicated comparison by 12/22. 3) Veridian to confirm golden prompt set and success criteria by 12/23. 4) Sourav to provide KMS/HSM requirements and data retention redline by 2026-01-03. 5) Tom to open network onboarding ticket for sandbox for shadow run and we'll schedule shadow routing next Wednesday 12/24 10:00 PST.
[07:01] Anika Patel: perfect, thank you.
[07:04] Tom Reynolds: thanks everyone.
[07:06] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up in the thread with the links. Bye.
